title: Sanitized interview answer
description: Local CP-03 contract. Version 1.0.0 is retained read-only; new writes use 1.1.0 with one bounded last-correction marker. This schema does not execute or authorize side effects.
x-invariants: Sanitization recognizes only the named synthetic canaries in x-sanitizer-contract. It is not a general secret detector and does not prove arbitrary confidential prose safe.

Match case-sensitively and longest-first. The assignment is one match; a block is one contiguous match from the begin delimiter through the next end delimiter. Replace each match with [REDACTED], collapse adjacent redactions separated only by whitespace, normalize CRLF or CR to LF, and trim only outer whitespace. Do not otherwise normalize Unicode or interior whitespace.

Measure the sanitized answer in Unicode code points. More than 2000 code points fails invalid_input without truncation or commit. Empty or fully redacted output fails invalid_input, keeps the pending question unchanged and returns message key answer_fully_redacted.

Raw named canaries never enter state, finalized history, recovery or pending files, stdout, stderr, publication results or runtime-preflight results. redaction_applied is true exactly when a named-canary replacement occurred.

For 1.1.0, an initial answer has last_correction_id=null. A pre-Brief correction updates the existing answer in place with the same answer_id, question_id and ordinal, increments answer_revision by one, records the correction ID in last_correction_id, and retains only the current sanitized answer rather than raw or prior-answer history. It does not create a user-corrections event or Brief version.

Correction payload identity is the canonical sanitized mutation tuple: correction ID, expected state revision, run/answer/question IDs, ordinal, status, sanitized_value and redaction_applied. Under the state lock, an incoming ID equal to last_correction_id is a no-op only when current state revision equals expected_state_revision + 1, the saved answer expected_state_revision matches, and every other tuple field equals the saved current answer; that ID with a different tuple returns state_conflict. A different ID applies only when expected_state_revision is current. After any later commit, an unchanged older replay has a stale expected revision and is state_conflict; callers must not rebase an old ID onto a new expected revision, because that is a new payload and requires a new ID. This bounded marker does not claim historical-ID lookup.
